claims.claimText: Waterloo AVPA guidance on Applying UW Principles of AI Enablement to Teaching and Learning states that GenAI use must consider data security, prohibiting uploading student work or course materials to insecure AI tools, and specifying that student information such as identification or grades is subject to Policy 46 (Information Management) and must not be uploaded to AI tools that do not meet institutional security requirements.
claims.claimValue: Student work, course materials, and student information (Policy 46) must not be uploaded to insecure AI tools.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: GenAI use in teaching and learning must consider the security of student data, course materials, and other intellectual property. Instructors and students must select AI tools that provide an appropriate level of data protection, following university guidance. Neither course materials nor student work should be uploaded to insecure AI tools that might share them without permission. Student information such as identification or grades is subject to Policy 46 – Information Management and must not be uploaded to AI tools that do not meet institutional security requirements.
evidence.snippetLocation: Safe & fair use: Responsible, ethical, inclusive AI

claims.claimText: Waterloo's Academic Integrity page says instructors should state whether AI tools such as ChatGPT are allowed for assignments, tests, or exams, and that students who do not follow those instructor rules are subject to Policy 71 academic-misconduct processes.
claims.claimValue: Instructor-defined AI-use rules are tied to Policy 71 compliance.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: At present, it's important for instructors to be explicit about whether artificial intelligence or tools like ChatGPT are allowed to be used to complete assignments, tests or exams, and if so, the extent to which it is allowed, and if it should be cited and how to cite it. A student who does not comply with the instructor's rules about the use of such tools will be subject to Policy 71 and an investigation into academic misconduct.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: Academic Integrity tells instructors to state whether AI tools are allowed and links noncompliance to Policy 71.
evidence.snippetLocation: Instructor resources for Artificial Intelligence ChatGPT tools

claims.claimText: Waterloo's graduate-student GenAI guidance says graduate students should not submit GenAI-produced work for course assignments without explicit course-instructor permission or instruction.
claims.claimValue: Graduate coursework GenAI use depends on instructor permission.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Without explicit permission or instruction from the course instructor, students should never submit work produced by any of the GenAI tools.

claims.claimText: For units or individuals deploying AI-enabled systems that process University data, Waterloo IST says projects must undergo an Information Risk Assessment and receive Information Steward approval before using University data.
claims.claimValue: AI-enabled systems processing University data require IRA and Information Steward approval.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: All AI-enabled system projects must undergo an Information Risk Assessment (IRA). A Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) may also be required, depending on the nature of the data being collected or processed. Approval from the appropriate Information Steward is required before using any University data, even if that data is publicly available.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: IST says AI-enabled system projects require an IRA, may require a PIA, and need steward approval before University data use.

claims.claimText: For graduate research contexts, Waterloo's GenAI guidance directs graduate students to consult supervisors and, when applicable, advisory committees about the limits and scope of GenAI-tool use.
claims.claimValue: Graduate research GenAI use should be discussed with supervisors or advisory committees.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: For research, graduate students should consult with their supervisor(s) and advisory committee (if one exists) about the limit and scope of the use of GenAI tools, which is often discipline-dependent. Permitted uses and expectations for using GenAI tools should be communicated between the students and their supervisor(s).
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: Graduate guidance says research GenAI limits and scope should be discussed with supervisors and advisory committees where applicable.
